title: Tiny Hat: a new Linux distro dedicated to retro gamedev
summary:
Tiny Hat uses only around 100MB of RAM after booting, and can be booted from a >= 1GB memory stick. It comes with a few small games, an easy way to install and run more games and several example programs for getting into retro game development. It also uses a modern stack of libraries, with dwl / Wayland, SDL3 and GTK4.

One possible use is to buy a cheap x86 machine for younger members of a family, to completely brain wash inspire them into getting into graphics programming and appreciating retro games, perhaps as a Christmas present.

At least a few people have found it fun so far, so I wanted to share it.

title: I built a browser test that proves when a mouse sensor loses tracking (and got my refund with it)
summary:
Short story long, I bought a budget gaming mouse and something felt off in Valorant: slow aiming was fine, but hard flicks moved the crosshair far less than my hand did, and sometimes it snapped backwards. The usual online mouse testers check buttons, double-clicks and polling rate. None of them could show the seller what was actually happening.

So I built one that can.

The idea

If the mouse moves the exact same physical distance every time, a healthy sensor reports the same number of counts, no matter how fast you move. So:

  1. Put two hard stops on the mousepad (books, a ruler, the pad's edges).
  2. Do a few slow swipes between them. Their median becomes the baseline.
  3. Flick hard between the same stops.
  4. Any fast swipe more than 10% off the baseline is flagged: SHORT (lost movement), LONG (added movement) or spin-out (movement reported backwards).

Why

I publish Android apps and wanted one number per keyword, per country, per day, without buying a full ASO suite. So I built Rankfy.

How it works

  • For Google Play, Rankfy requests the public search page for a keyword with the country (gl) and language (hl) set, and reads the apps in the order the store returns them.
  • For the App Store, it uses the public iTunes Search API with the country code.
  • Your position is your index in that list. A scheduled job repeats the check every day and stores the history.
  • No paid data source is involved, which is why it cannot tell you search volume.

title: Why Optimistic UI Updates Make Your Apps Feel Instant
summary:
What Are Optimistic UI Updates?

An optimistic UI update is a frontend design pattern where a web application immediately updates its screen to show the result of a user's action before getting confirmation from the backend server. Instead of freezing the screen or displaying a loading spinner while waiting for a network request—the process of sending data across the internet to a remote server—the app acts optimistic. It predicts that the server request will succeed 99% of the time, updates the interface instantly, and syncs with the database in the background. If the request unexpectedly fails, the app catches the error and silently rolls the user interface back to its original state.

Ask Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex to scaffold a 2D dungeon platformer in Godot 4, Unity, or Phaser 3 and it will write working movement, collisions, and camera code in five minutes.

Then look at the sprites.

title: Only p99 is slow while iostat looks normal: the cause is a cgroup IOPS limit
summary:
In the read times measured by an application, the median stays where it usually is, but only the upper percentiles such as p99 (the value at the 99% position when the times are sorted from fastest to slowest) jump to around 100ms.

iostat -x for the same period shows an r_await (the average wait per read) far below the values that jumped, and a low %util (the fraction of time the disk was processing something).

If you see this combination, suspect a cgroup read limit. A cgroup is the kernel mechanism that groups processes and places limits on their CPU, memory, and I/O. Each systemd service and each Docker container is one cgroup.

Fuzz testing remains an effective tool for discovering software defects, more so than ever with AI agents driving, fixing bugs on the fly, clearing the way for deeper fuzzing, all unattended.
